prompts.title: Option A — Project workbench
prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished, high fidelity Windows desktop AMR engineering application concept screenshot. Landscape 16:10 composition, preferably 1920 x 1200 or greater. Full front-on application UI, no photographed monitor, no perspective, no decorative device frame. This is a proposed future interface for approval, not an implemented product. Prominent small header badge must read "CONCEPT · SAMPLE DATA". Product title "AMR Engineering". Project title "Reference hospital.amrproj". Engineering modellers, not consumers. Calm practical desktop design, crisp legible typography, generous spacing, high contrast dark navy text on light surfaces, blue primary accent, restrained amber warnings; no gradients, no glossy marketing decoration. Accessible design includes named routes and different line patterns, never colour alone. Use a simple recognisable floor-plan diagram with straight corridors, three clearly named destinations "Stores", "Ward A", "Waste", a labelled "Shared corridor", blue solid "Clean" route and orange dashed "Dirty" route. Label the shared part explicitly and use both route strokes there. Door and robot icons, discrete node dots, dimensions in metres. Floor plan is schematic sample geometry, no real hospital drawing. Main workflow is Project → Layout → Configuration → Check → Simulate → Review → Report; preserve all seven named stages. Include "Text size" and "Theme" controls, clear save/undo affordances and an unobtrusive help button. Avoid tiny dense text: prioritise a few readable rows. Include a narrow footer explicitly reading "Illustrative concept — not validation evidence". Never label the example certified or fully verified. Layout should look technically plausible and buildable in PySide6. Show useful user-facing controls, no source code, hashes, JSON paths or implementation jargon. OPTION A: persistent project-tree workbench. Title strip subtitle "A · Project workbench". Top slim app/menu bar and compact command toolbar. Left 18% width persistent navigation tree listing all seven stages, Layout selected, expanded floor 0 with Routes and Doors; small project revision and save status. Centre 57% width dominant editable floor layout, slim local toolbar "Draw corridor", "Insert node", "Split link", "Snap". Right 25% width contextual inspector headed "Door D-03", fields "Clear width 1.20 m", "Route profiles Clean, Dirty", compact "Apply" and "Cancel" buttons. Highlight this door on the map. Bottom centre dock approximately 18% height labelled "Project checks", containing two concise warnings with object names and a "Go to object" action, and button "Run checks". Controls should make it obvious that selecting an object edits its properties without a modal dialog, and that checked findings return to the selected object. Keep the map useful in spite of the bottom dock. Do not use large cards. This is a professional flexible workbench with direct stage switching. Common CAD interaction requirements: a clearly grouped toolbar for "Select", "Polyline", "Node", "Location", "Door", "Trim", "Fillet"; a Layers and line types control with named continuous and dashed patterns. A crosshair cursor and a small drawing preview with dimensions show familiar CAD behaviour. Footer toggles labelled "Snap", "Grid", "Ortho", "Units: m", with a compact command/prompt strip such as "Specify next point or enter length". Include unobtrusive keyboard hint "Esc cancel · Enter finish". Location tools place editable labelled footprints, not only anonymous graph points. Nodes and edges have selectable grips; drawing an engineering route should feel like CAD. Line type is a display property; Clean/Dirty/Shared routing permissions are separate named profiles. Illustrate these controls without overcrowding the seven-stage application.

prompts.title: Common CAD drawing interactions
prompts.prompt: Use case ui-mockup. Create a high fidelity instructional design board for a proposed Windows desktop AMR engineering CAD editor, landscape 16:10 at high resolution. White/light grey background, crisp navy text and blue accents with orange dashed secondary routes. Title "CAD drawing workflow · for approval", small badge "CONCEPT · SAMPLE DATA". Four equally sized panels in a two-by-two grid, each a cropped plausible editable floorplan canvas with a small related CAD toolbar or properties strip. Number each panel with large readable title. Panel 1 "1 Draw a corridor": crosshair, polyline with three placed vertices and one ghost preview segment, dimension "4.00 m", dynamic length entry, footer "Click next point · Enter finish · Esc cancel"; toolbar Polyline, Snap, Ortho. Panel 2 "2 Insert and connect a node": a highlighted existing corridor edge, midpoint snap square, new clearly labelled Node N-04, two resulting linked segments, caption "Snap to edge → insert node → split and reconnect"; show selection grips and no geometry disconnected. Panel 3 "3 Place a location": a rectangular location footprint labelled "Ward A", dragged corner sizing grip, rotation handle, one visible connection/anchor node, dimensions "3.00 m × 2.00 m"; properties "Name", "Type", "Rotation", sensible short sample values. Panel 4 "4 Edit line and turn properties": selected corridor with corner radius arc labelled "R 1.50 m" and dashed loaded footprint envelope; properties rows "Layer: Corridors", "Line type: Dashed", "Width: 2.40 m", "Route profiles: Clean, Dirty"; caption "Line style changes appearance; profiles control access." Show tiny one-step undo affordance. Use engineering CAD graphic conventions, axis marker, grips, snap markers and metre dimensions. Routes use both labels and line patterns for accessibility. Footer "Proposed interactions — geometry and accessibility require implementation tests". This is a design approval concept, no claims of existing implementation or certified geometry. Keep text readable, no photographs, device frames, perspective, code or marketing graphics.

revisions.prompt: Edit only the two warning messages in the bottom Project checks table of this UI concept. Preserve all layout, colours, controls and floorplan pixels as closely as possible. Replace the first message with "Review loaded clearance at door D-02." Replace the second message with "Review permissions on the Waste route." Do not invent universal minimum door widths or mandatory redundant routes. Keep the CONCEPT SAMPLE DATA badge and footer. Everything else unchanged.

Edit only the bottom amber readiness notice and the Layers / Line types labels of this UI concept. Preserve the entire application layout and floorplan. The floorplan already contains three locations, so replace "Layout needs two locations" with "Finish corridor drawing" and its subtitle with "Press Enter to finish, or Esc to cancel." Keep Continue to Configuration disabled while drawing. In Layers / Line types, replace "Clean (solid)" with "Corridors (continuous)", replace "Dirty (dashed)" with "Annotations (dashed)", and replace "Shared (both)" with "Route profiles: Clean, Dirty". Line type display settings must not define routing permission. All other elements unchanged.

Make these targeted edits to this comparison-workspace concept while preserving the overall layout, maps, timeline and colours. In BOTH maps properties areas, change the routing heading to "Route profiles (allowed)". Replace checkbox labels "Clean robots" with "Clean", and "Dirty robots" with "Dirty". REMOVE the separate "Shared (both)" checkbox entirely; replace it with plain noninteractive text "Shared access: Clean + Dirty". Shared access is membership in both profiles, never a third classification switch. On the RIGHT saved-run pane, grey out and visibly disable Polyline, Node, Location, Door, Trim and Fillet; keep Select usable. The right pane is read only. In its bottom properties area fields and checkboxes remain disabled. Add small playback controls with a play triangle and horizontal time scrubber at the bottom of the right map, without covering the legend. Everything else remains a design concept with the existing badges.

graph_refinement.prompt: Edit this approved-direction AMR Engineering desktop UI concept to make the graph canvas dominate the main window. Preserve its overall Windows CAD workbench look, light theme, typography, blue accent, product title, seven named workflow stages, route colours/patterns, same floor plan and illustrative badge. Keep landscape aspect ratio. New version subtitle "A2 · Graph-focused workbench". Reconfigure the layout as follows: reduce left project tree to a slim roughly 12 percent width dock, still showing Project, Layout, floor 0, Routes, Nodes, Doors, Locations and remaining workflow stages; use short names and compact rows. Completely COLLAPSE the large right Door properties panel into a thin right-edge vertical tab reading "Properties", with a small pin/expand icon. Do not show an expanded form. Completely COLLAPSE the bottom Project checks table into a single slim bar reading "Project checks · 2 warnings" with "Open checks" at right; the graph now extends almost to the bottom command bar. The graph area should occupy about 80 percent of available workspace below the toolbars. Expand the central canvas to use all reclaimed space; make the floor plan comfortably large with useful white/grid space around it, no cropped rooms. Keep a selected door D-03 and a very small unobtrusive selection label "Door D-03 · 1.20 m" on the canvas, not a floating full form. Keep just one compact CAD toolbar row (Select, Polyline, Node, Location, Door, Trim, Fillet, Layers, Line type) above the canvas. Keep drawing prompt, Snap/Grid/Ortho, metre units and coordinate controls in a single compact bottom status bar. Add a small "Focus canvas" control near the canvas top-right. The key requirement is a graph-first CAD workbench: side/bottom panels are supplemental, user-expandable and never crowd the default drawing view. No large properties form, no checks table, no dashboard cards in this default state. Preserve labels that distinguish Clean and Dirty routes and explicitly shared sections, with no separate shared classification checkbox. Maintain footer "Illustrative concept — not validation evidence". This is a design refinement, not a real screenshot; keep "CONCEPT · SAMPLE DATA".
